title: Cardiovascular event rate modifies response to pharmacologic LDL-C lowering in primary prevention: implications of a systematic review and meta-analysis for clinical practice
notice: This bundled record demonstrates the native AJPC reader using verified article metadata and a concise summary. Run the included PMC synchronization script to replace it with the complete JATS-derived article body, figures, tables, and references.

abstract.text: Across 17 randomized trials and 105,879 participants, lower-risk primary-prevention populations derived greater relative cardiovascular benefit per unit of LDL-C reduction, supporting earlier, risk-informed treatment.

blocks.text: This page is rendered entirely on the AJPC website. After the article synchronization script is run, the same layout displays the complete PMC JATS record without sending readers to ScienceDirect or PMC.
The importer preserves article sections, paragraphs, lists, figures, tables, references, DOI and PMCID provenance, and the Creative Commons attribution statement.

The analysis evaluated randomized trials of pharmacologic LDL-C lowering in primary prevention and examined whether baseline cardiovascular event rates modified the relative benefit associated with LDL-C reduction.

items: Earlier treatment in lower-risk populations was associated with greater relative benefit per unit of LDL-C reduction
